source: WRAP UK / Defra Organic Waste Conversion Benchmark (Illustrative prototype data)
caveat: Assumes low physical contamination (<3% non-organics) and balanced volatile solids. Higher oil/fats content increases yield toward the upper bound but requires mesophilic temperature stability.

source: International Energy Agency (IEA) Bioenergy Task 37 Table 4.2 (Illustrative prototype data)
caveat: High inherent water content reduces biogas yield per fresh tonne. Requires mechanical maceration to prevent fibrous floating crust in smaller digesters.

source: European Biomass Industry Association (EUBIA) Feedstock Guide (Illustrative prototype data)
caveat: Prone to rapid acidification (VFA accumulation) if fed without buffering. Co-digestion with alkaline manure or pH control chemicals is strongly recommended.

source: Anaerobic Digestion and Bioresources Association (ADBA) Feedstock Metric (Illustrative prototype data)
caveat: Relatively low energy density due to 88-92% water content. Provides essential biological buffering, micronutrients, and liquid vehicle when co-digested with solid food waste.
